title: PROGRAM-ID not recorded when its separator period is missing
shapes: PROGRAM-ID.    LNRATE + blanks to col 72, no period after the name (LNRATE)
PROGRAM-ID LNCALC. (no period after the keyword) (LNCALC)
asserts: The program-name is LNRATE / LNCALC: PROGRAM-ID names the program whatever the punctuation around it.

citations.doc: Enterprise COBOL for z/OS 6.4 Language Reference

lower_confidence: IBM's syntax diagram shows both periods as required. That Enterprise COBOL compiles the period-less forms with a diagnostic rests on #4307's evidence (cobol-programming-course CBLDB22 compiles in its own JCL), not on an IBM sentence. The fact the key asserts, the program-name, does not depend on it. Both members are IBM-only here; the check compiles a variant with the periods restored.
notes: LNRATE has no AUTHOR paragraph, as #4307's CBLDB22 has none: when a period-terminated AUTHOR. line follows the period-less PROGRAM-ID, the engine records the name, which would hide shape 1.

compile.reason: PROGRAM-ID keyword with no separator period (Enterprise COBOL diagnoses and continues; GnuCOBOL -std=ibm rejects it)
compile.check_note: the PROGRAM-ID line is rewritten to `PROGRAM-ID. <name>.` for the check; everything else compiles as written
